options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Agricultural productivity doubles when common pastures are unregulated

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Environmental and Natural Resource Economics (Tragedy of the Commons):
Individual users acting independently and rationally according to self-interest deplete shared, open-access resources, harming common welfare

Detailed Context:
Detailed Solution:

Hardin's Tragedy of the Commons shows that when a resource is shared, open-access, and rival (like oceans, atmosphere, or common pastures), individual self-interest leads to over-exploitation and eventual collapse of the resource for all.

Hence, Option (B) 

Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.

topic: Geological Genesis of Coal from Ancient Swamp Flora
questionText:
Arrange the stages of geological coalification over hundreds of millions of years under heat and pressure:
(I) Dense ancient swamp forests and giant lycophyte ferns die, accumulating in stagnant, oxygen-poor water basins
(II) Partial microbial decomposition in anaerobic mire forms spongy, high-moisture 'Peat'
(III) Burial beneath thousands of meters of sedimentary rock compresses peat into brown, soft 'Lignite'
(IV) Intense tectonic thermal maturation and overburden pressure convert lignite into hard 'Bituminous' and finally metamorphic 'Anthracite' coal

Choose the correct chronological/logical sequence from the options given below:

options.text: I -> II -> III -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.

options.text: I -> III -> II -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: II -> I -> III -> IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: IV -> II -> III -> I
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Coal formation: swamp accumulation, anaerobic peat formation, sedimentary compression into lignite, and thermal maturation into bituminous/anthracite.
Hence Option D is correct.
Hence, option (A) is correct.
